title: Aquaculture Systems & Pond Management
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 300L Aquaculture Systems & Pond Management curriculum: types of aquaculture systems (earthen ponds, concrete/tank culture, cages), pond site selection and construction, water quality management, liming and fertilization, stocking density, feeding management, monoculture versus polyculture, and harvesting. Kept distinct from Advanced Aquaculture (FIS401), which covers advanced/high-tech systems, genetics, and RAS, and from Integrated Fish Farming (FIS407), which covers fish-livestock/crop integration specifically.

questions.question: An earthen pond, the most common aquaculture system in Nigeria, is primarily constructed from:
options: Compacted soil with a dyke/embankment to retain water
Reinforced concrete slabs only
Welded steel panels
Woven plastic mesh over a wooden frame
questions.correct_answer: Compacted soil with a dyke/embankment to retain water
questions.explanation: Earthen ponds are excavated and/or embanked from compacted soil, relying on the soil's water-holding capacity, and are the most widely used and cost-effective culture system in Nigerian aquaculture.

questions.question: A key advantage of concrete or tank-based fish culture systems over earthen ponds is:
options: Easier water quality control and reduced risk of pond wall erosion or seepage
Complete elimination of the need for feeding
Lower construction cost than earthen ponds in every case
No need for any water source at all
questions.correct_answer: Easier water quality control and reduced risk of pond wall erosion or seepage
questions.explanation: Concrete or tank systems allow more precise control over water exchange and quality and avoid the seepage, erosion, and burrowing predator issues associated with earthen ponds, though they are typically more expensive to construct.

questions.question: Cage culture, as a fish farming system, involves:
options: Rearing fish in a mesh enclosure suspended within a larger natural or man-made water body
Growing fish entirely on dry land with no water
Using only recirculating pumps with no netting
Culturing fish exclusively in glass aquaria
questions.correct_answer: Rearing fish in a mesh enclosure suspended within a larger natural or man-made water body
questions.explanation: Cage culture confines fish within a netted enclosure placed in an existing water body such as a lake, reservoir, or river, allowing free water exchange through the mesh while containing the stock.

questions.question: When selecting a site for pond construction, soil with a high clay content is generally preferred because it:
options: Has good water-retention properties, minimizing seepage losses
Allows water to drain away quickly
Prevents any aquatic plant growth
Cannot support pond dyke construction
questions.correct_answer: Has good water-retention properties, minimizing seepage losses
questions.explanation: Clayey soils compact well and have low permeability, reducing water loss through seepage, which is essential for maintaining stable water levels in earthen ponds.

questions.question: An important consideration in pond site selection regarding water supply is that the site should have:
options: A reliable, adequate, and good-quality water source throughout the production cycle
No access to any water source
Only floodwater available during the rainy season
Water with very high salinity regardless of species cultured
questions.correct_answer: A reliable, adequate, and good-quality water source throughout the production cycle
questions.explanation: A dependable supply of adequate quantity and quality water is essential for filling, topping up, and exchanging pond water throughout the culture period.

questions.question: The primary purpose of a pond's inlet and outlet structures is to:
options: Control water flow into and out of the pond, including draining for harvest
Provide feeding stations for fish
Serve as the pond's main aeration source
Store harvested fish before sale
questions.correct_answer: Control water flow into and out of the pond, including draining for harvest
questions.explanation: Inlet and outlet (drainage) structures allow the pond manager to fill, exchange, and fully drain the pond, which is essential for water quality management and harvesting.

questions.question: Liming a fish pond with agricultural lime before stocking primarily serves to:
options: Raise pond soil and water pH and improve water productivity
Increase the salinity of the pond
Eliminate the need for any fertilization
Immediately kill all fish already stocked
questions.correct_answer: Raise pond soil and water pH and improve water productivity
questions.explanation: Liming neutralizes acidic pond soils, raises pH toward optimal ranges, and improves nutrient availability, ultimately enhancing natural productivity and water quality.

questions.question: Pond fertilization, using organic manure or inorganic fertilizer, is applied mainly to:
options: Stimulate phytoplankton and natural food organism production
Directly kill unwanted predatory fish
Reduce the pond's water level
Sterilize the pond bottom completely
questions.correct_answer: Stimulate phytoplankton and natural food organism production
questions.explanation: Fertilization adds nutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus) that boost phytoplankton and zooplankton growth, increasing natural food available to fish, especially important in extensive and semi-intensive systems.

questions.question: An extensive aquaculture system is characterized by:
options: Low stocking density with reliance mainly on natural pond productivity for food
Very high stocking density requiring complete artificial feed
Fully automated water recirculation with zero natural inputs
Culture exclusively in glass tanks indoors
questions.correct_answer: Low stocking density with reliance mainly on natural pond productivity for food
questions.explanation: Extensive systems use low stocking densities and depend largely on naturally occurring food organisms in the pond, with little or no supplementary feeding or input.

questions.question: Intensive aquaculture systems are characterized mainly by:
options: High stocking densities with complete dependence on formulated feed and active water quality management
Extremely low stocking densities with no feeding
The complete absence of any water quality monitoring
Reliance solely on wild-caught fingerlings with no hatchery input
questions.correct_answer: High stocking densities with complete dependence on formulated feed and active water quality management
questions.explanation: Intensive systems stock fish at high densities and depend on nutritionally complete formulated feed along with active aeration and water exchange to sustain water quality.

questions.question: Semi-intensive aquaculture systems typically combine:
options: Moderate stocking density with both natural pond food and supplementary feeding
Zero stocking with only wild fish entering naturally
Extremely high densities with no feed input at all
Culture exclusively in floating netted cages in the ocean
questions.correct_answer: Moderate stocking density with both natural pond food and supplementary feeding
questions.explanation: Semi-intensive systems occupy a middle ground, using moderate stocking densities supported by a combination of natural pond productivity (often boosted by fertilization) and supplementary feed.

questions.question: Stocking density in aquaculture refers to:
options: The number or weight of fish stocked per unit area or volume of water
The total market value of fish in a pond
The number of pond workers assigned per hectare
The distance between adjacent ponds
questions.correct_answer: The number or weight of fish stocked per unit area or volume of water
questions.explanation: Stocking density expresses how many fish (by number or biomass) are placed per unit of pond area or water volume, a key variable affecting growth, water quality, and yield.

questions.question: Overstocking a pond beyond its carrying capacity most directly leads to:
options: Reduced individual growth rates and deteriorating water quality
Automatically faster individual fish growth
Elimination of the need for feeding
Permanent improvement in dissolved oxygen levels
questions.correct_answer: Reduced individual growth rates and deteriorating water quality
questions.explanation: When stocking density exceeds a pond's carrying capacity, competition for food and oxygen increases, water quality (especially dissolved oxygen and ammonia) deteriorates, and individual growth slows.

questions.question: Monoculture in fish farming refers to:
options: Rearing a single fish species in a pond or system
Rearing multiple complementary species together in one pond
Growing fish alongside crops only
Culturing fish only in cages, never in ponds
questions.correct_answer: Rearing a single fish species in a pond or system
questions.explanation: Monoculture is the practice of culturing only one species at a time in a given system, simplifying management but not exploiting the full range of pond niches.

questions.question: Polyculture, as practiced in some Nigerian pond systems, involves:
options: Rearing two or more compatible fish species together to make efficient use of different ecological niches
Rearing only one species but in multiple separate ponds
Rotating a single species through different water bodies each week
Growing fish and plants with no ecological interaction
questions.correct_answer: Rearing two or more compatible fish species together to make efficient use of different ecological niches
questions.explanation: Polyculture combines species with differing feeding habits (e.g., a surface feeder with a bottom feeder) in the same pond to make more complete use of available natural food and space, increasing total yield.

questions.question: A commonly cited advantage of polyculture over monoculture is:
options: More efficient use of available food niches, often increasing total pond yield
Complete elimination of any need for water quality monitoring
Guaranteed absence of disease in all species
Simpler harvesting because all fish are identical
questions.correct_answer: More efficient use of available food niches, often increasing total pond yield
questions.explanation: By combining species that exploit different feeding niches (plankton feeders, bottom feeders, herbivores), polyculture can increase overall biomass production per unit area compared to a single species alone.

questions.question: Dissolved oxygen is typically at its lowest level in a fish pond at which time of day?
options: Early morning, just before sunrise
Mid-afternoon
Immediately after fertilization
Exactly at noon
questions.correct_answer: Early morning, just before sunrise
questions.explanation: Overnight, phytoplankton and other organisms consume oxygen through respiration without photosynthetic replenishment, so dissolved oxygen is lowest just before sunrise, making this a critical monitoring time.

questions.question: A pond dissolved oxygen level that is chronically too low can be corrected by:
options: Mechanical aeration or increased water exchange
Adding more fish to the pond
Reducing water depth to zero
Stopping all feeding permanently with no other action
questions.correct_answer: Mechanical aeration or increased water exchange
questions.explanation: Paddlewheel aerators, air blowers, or increased water exchange are standard interventions to raise dissolved oxygen when natural production and diffusion are insufficient.

questions.question: Ammonia toxicity is a major water quality concern in intensive fish culture mainly because it:
options: Accumulates from fish excretion and uneaten feed, impairing gill function and growth at high levels
Is beneficial to fish at any concentration
Only occurs in marine systems, never in ponds
Has no relationship to feeding rate
questions.correct_answer: Accumulates from fish excretion and uneaten feed, impairing gill function and growth at high levels
questions.explanation: Ammonia is excreted by fish and produced by decomposing uneaten feed and waste; at elevated concentrations it damages gill tissue and suppresses growth and immune function.

questions.question: Feeding rate in pond aquaculture is commonly expressed as a percentage of:
options: Fish body weight per day
Total pond water volume
Pond surface area
Number of workers on the farm
questions.correct_answer: Fish body weight per day
questions.explanation: Feeding rates are typically set as a percentage of estimated total fish biomass per day (e.g., 3-5% body weight/day), adjusted as fish grow.

questions.question: Feed conversion ratio (FCR) in aquaculture is calculated as:
options: Weight of feed given divided by weight gain of fish
Weight gain of fish divided by weight of feed given
Total feed cost divided by total fish sold
Number of fish stocked divided by number harvested
questions.correct_answer: Weight of feed given divided by weight gain of fish
questions.explanation: FCR = feed input / weight gain, and a lower FCR indicates more efficient conversion of feed into fish biomass.

questions.question: Overfeeding in pond aquaculture is problematic primarily because uneaten feed:
options: Decomposes and degrades water quality while wasting money
Automatically improves fish growth with no downside
Has no effect on pond ecology
Increases dissolved oxygen levels
questions.correct_answer: Decomposes and degrades water quality while wasting money
questions.explanation: Uneaten feed decomposes, consuming oxygen and releasing ammonia, which degrades water quality, while also representing wasted expenditure on an input that was not converted to fish growth.

questions.question: Regular sampling of fish (weighing a subset of the population) during the grow-out period is done mainly to:
options: Monitor growth and adjust feeding rates accordingly
Permanently remove fish from the pond before harvest
Replace the need for water quality testing
Determine the exact market price of the fish
questions.correct_answer: Monitor growth and adjust feeding rates accordingly
questions.explanation: Periodic sampling estimates average fish weight and total biomass, allowing farmers to recalculate feeding rates and track growth performance over the culture cycle.

questions.question: Total draining of a pond as a harvesting method is advantageous mainly because it:
options: Allows complete harvest of all fish and facilitates pond bottom drying and preparation for the next cycle
Is the only method that can be used for cage culture
Prevents any need for grading fish
Eliminates the need for a water source entirely
questions.correct_answer: Allows complete harvest of all fish and facilitates pond bottom drying and preparation for the next cycle
questions.explanation: Draining the pond concentrates and allows total harvest of the stock while exposing the pond bottom, which can then be dried, limed, and prepared for the next production cycle.

questions.question: Partial harvesting using seine nets, as opposed to complete draining, is useful when a farmer wants to:
options: Selectively remove market-size fish while leaving smaller fish to continue growing
Permanently close the pond after one harvest
Avoid handling any fish at all
Harvest only dead fish from the pond
questions.correct_answer: Selectively remove market-size fish while leaving smaller fish to continue growing
questions.explanation: Seine (drag) netting allows farmers to catch larger, market-ready fish while releasing smaller individuals back into the pond to continue growing, without fully draining the system.

questions.question: A nursery pond in a fish farming operation is specifically used to:
options: Rear fry and fingerlings to a larger size before stocking into grow-out ponds
House only broodstock for breeding
Store harvested market-size fish before sale
Process fish into smoked or dried products
questions.correct_answer: Rear fry and fingerlings to a larger size before stocking into grow-out ponds
questions.explanation: Nursery ponds provide a controlled, protected environment for rearing delicate fry and fingerlings to a more robust size before transfer to larger grow-out ponds, improving survival.

questions.question: A dyke (embankment) in earthen pond construction must be properly compacted mainly to:
options: Prevent seepage and structural failure that could lead to water loss or dyke collapse
Increase the pond's dissolved oxygen level
Serve as a substitute for fertilization
Eliminate the need for an inlet structure
questions.correct_answer: Prevent seepage and structural failure that could lead to water loss or dyke collapse
questions.explanation: Poorly compacted dykes are prone to seepage, erosion, and even collapse under water pressure, so proper compaction during construction is essential for pond integrity.

questions.question: Turbid (muddy) pond water resulting from suspended soil particles can be problematic because it:
options: Reduces light penetration needed for phytoplankton photosynthesis, lowering natural productivity
Always increases fish growth rates
Has no effect on primary productivity
Automatically raises the pond's pH to ideal levels
questions.correct_answer: Reduces light penetration needed for phytoplankton photosynthesis, lowering natural productivity
questions.explanation: High turbidity from suspended clay or silt blocks light needed for phytoplankton photosynthesis, reducing the natural food base and oxygen production in the pond.

questions.question: The recommended practice of drying and exposing a pond bottom to sunlight between production cycles primarily helps to:
options: Oxidize organic matter, kill pathogens, and mineralize nutrients in the sediment
Increase the pond's water depth
Eliminate the need for future liming
Prevent any fish from ever being restocked
questions.correct_answer: Oxidize organic matter, kill pathogens, and mineralize nutrients in the sediment
questions.explanation: Sun-drying the pond bottom oxidizes accumulated organic matter, helps mineralize nutrients for the next cycle, and reduces populations of pathogens and unwanted organisms in the sediment.

questions.question: A fish farmer choosing between monoculture of Clarias gariepinus and polyculture with Oreochromis niloticus should consider that:
options: Clarias is carnivorous/predatory and may prey on small tilapia, so compatibility and size grading matter in polyculture
The two species can never be reared in the same water body under any circumstances
Tilapia will always outcompete and eliminate Clarias regardless of size
There is no ecological interaction between the two species
questions.correct_answer: Clarias is carnivorous/predatory and may prey on small tilapia, so compatibility and size grading matter in polyculture
questions.explanation: Because Clarias is predatory, combining it with tilapia requires careful consideration of relative sizes and stocking strategy to avoid the catfish preying excessively on smaller tilapia, though controlled polyculture combinations are used in practice.
